excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: RULED 2026-10-27 AFTER THE FULL LADDER, AND THE ZERO IS A MEASUREMENT WITH A RING-FENCE RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE. THE CONSTRUCT: `renders` is source = the rendering symbol, target = the rendered COMPONENT, and the host renderer constructs the element (src/ast/types.ts). Haskell has no component model at all: no declaration denotes a component, nothing constructs an element, and there is no host renderer to attribute the construction to. MEASURED over the WHOLE admitted population (3,702 .hs/.lhs files over 6 repositories, engine.getParser -> parse -> analyze, 3,702 parsed of 3,702, 0 failures) by script/m14/haskell-extended-census.ts, artifact validation/m14/measurements/haskell-extended-census.json: templateLoaderSplices = 0 — the nearest analogue in the whole language, a Template Haskell loader that names a template FILE, has 0 sites, and even where it exists it names a FILE rather than a component symbol, so this vocabulary has nothing to bind. THE RING-FENCE, COUNTED SO THE RULING IS FALSIFIABLE: 4,201 quasiquote sites (`[hamlet|...|]`, `[blaze|...|]` are markup PRODUCERS — an expression evaluates to markup and applies no component), 0 of which render a declared component; 30 ANN pragmas (passive metadata); 420 declaration-position TH splices (already the `decorates` population, none naming a component). FALSIFIER: a corpus site where a declaration produces a component value a host renderer constructs AND whose target is a declared component — 0 measured over 3,702 files. THE LADDER, WALKED AND NAMED: R1 (a published build whose inventory HAS the construct) is UNAVAILABLE — the served grammar is the newest release of a dormant grammar (tree-sitter-haskell 0.23.1, digest 37a6b07b1a83) and its 174 distinct named types of 552 ids contain no render/component/element node (validation/m14/measurements/haskell-grammar-nodes.json: the only match for any render-family stem is `view_pattern`, a GHC view-pattern node that is a pattern-synonym form and carries no relation); R2 (clone and patch) is UNAVAILABLE because a patch would have to INVENT a component model and a host renderer — syntax and semantics the language does not have — and a grammar change is a change to what a file can SAY, never to what the language MEANS; R3 (an existing node type) is UNAVAILABLE because no node type carries a component->component relation — the closest node types (`apply`, `quasiquote`, `top_splice`) are counted above and carry value production, not rendering. NOT `uses` AND NOT `instantiates`: a relabel of either would assert a name read or an allocation the source does not contain.

excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: RULED 2026-10-27 AFTER THE FULL LADDER, WITH THE NEAREST CONSTRUCT MEASURED AND READ THE OTHER WAY. THE CONSTRUCT: `mixes_in` is source = the composing type, target = the composed MEMBER SET, with no conformance declared (go struct embedding, zig `usingnamespace`, dart `with`, elixir `use`). Haskell has no such declaration: a type obtains an implementation only by DECLARING CONFORMANCE, and that family is already the three canonical values this lane emits — extends 189 edges over 64 files (superclass constraint), implements 13,721 over 974 (instance + deriving), overrides 1,274 over 91 (instance method). MEASURED over the WHOLE admitted population (3,702 files, 6 repositories, artifact validation/m14/measurements/haskell-extended-census.json): 360 class declarations, 12,451 instance declarations, 7,454 deriving clauses, 493 DerivingVia sites, 596 standalone deriving instances — every one a conformance construct, and 0 member-set compositions. THE SERVED GRAMMAR CONFIRMS THE ABSENCE AT THE INVENTORY LEVEL: 174 distinct named types (253 named slots) of 552 ids, digest 37a6b07b1a83 in validation/m14/measurements/haskell-grammar-nodes.json, and 0 of them is a mixin/trait/with/composition node (a stem probe over the whole inventory matches none). DERIVINGVIA IS THE ONE CONSTRUCT THAT LOOKS LIKE IT AND IS NOT, which is why this ruling is worth pinning: `deriving (Semigroup, Monoid) via (Sum Int)` makes a type obtain an implementation THROUGH a carrier type. The carrier supplies the INSTANCE, the type must still DECLARE the conformance (the analyzer reads it as `implements` with metadata.derived — validation/m14/fixtures/haskell/ruled-extended-types.hs, 2 rows on one clause), no member set is attached to the type, and the carrier is not a supertype. FALSIFIER: a corpus site where a declaration attaches a member set to a type without declaring conformance — 0 measured over 3,702 files. THE LADDER: R1 UNAVAILABLE (no published build carries the construct; the served build is the newest release of a dormant grammar and its inventory has none); R2 UNAVAILABLE because a patch would have to invent a construct the language has no syntax or semantics for — GHC's own answer to implementation reuse is a library plus deriving, a value-level and conformance-level mechanism, not a declaration the grammar could expose; R3 UNAVAILABLE because no existing node type carries a member-set composition, and the two candidates that could be MISREAD as one are measured above (deriving-via 493 sites; the superclass constraint, which is `extends`). NOT A RELABEL OF `implements`: a relabel would raise the ratio by moving 13,721 correctly-labelled conformance edges.

coverage._from: TEN OF TEN, MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE ADMITTED POPULATION, and this lane needs no exclusion. Reading: .tmp-covb/census.mts --lane haskell, a walk through the production path (engine.getParser -> RealHaskellAnalyzer.analyze) over 3,702 .hs/.lhs files (3,695 .hs + 7 .lhs) across 6 repos — 3,702 parsed of 3,702, 0 read failures, 0 parse throws, 0 analyze throws. Per-type totals: calls 57,682 edges in 1,777 files · contains 45,507 in 3,488 · imports 32,704 in 3,240 · instantiates 26,466 in 1,613 · exports 16,341 in 2,041 · implements 13,721 in 974 · uses 2,172 in 356 · overrides 1,274 in 91 · extends 189 in 64 · references 32 in 21. THE TWO SMALLEST, `references` (32) and `extends` (189), ARE SMALL AND MEASURED, NOT ZERO AND NOT ASSUMED: `extends` is the class-context constraint (6124 `=>` sites corpus-wide by the independent source-text probe, 189 of which became edges — the difference is the construct's other uses, not a failure of the count), and `references` is the qualified-name reference pass at 32 edges over 21 files. THIS BLOCK AGREES WITH `gap.gaps` RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT: HS-G1..HS-G10 are node-type gaps in advanced GHC-extension surfaces (type synonyms, GADTs, type/data families, FFI, Template Haskell, pattern synonyms, class defaults/fundeps, anonymous lambdas, deriving via, mdo) and NONE of them removes a relationship type; HS-G9 is the sharpest case and is a PARTIAL gap in an IMPLEMENTED type — `implements` fires 13,721 edges over 974 files while deriving-via strategies alone are not resolved. AND THE FIRING LOG'S ROW IS NOT A CONTRADICTION: validation/m14/results/firing-laptop-b.current.log reads `HASKELL 0 types fired  NO CORPUS under haskell` with all ten SILENT, a claim about the pin `haskell` (it admits 0 files at this HEAD) and not about the 3,702-file population measured here. DECORATES IS THE ELEVENTH IMPLEMENTED TYPE AND IT IS AN R3 EMISSION ON EXISTING NODE TYPES (the served grammar has `top_splice`, `splice`, `th_quoted_name`, `pragma`; validation/m14/measurements/haskell-grammar-nodes.json, served digest 37a6b07b1a83, 253 named of 552 ids). Template Haskell runs code at COMPILE TIME, so a DECLARATION-position splice is a real decorator application: `top_splice` whose expression applies a callable to a `th_quoted_name` naming a declaration THIS FILE declares. MEASURED over the whole admitted population by both instruments on the same 3,702 files: script/m14/haskell-extended-census.ts (all 420 rows inspected; validation/m14/measurements/haskell-extended-census.json) = 420 declaration-position splices, 344 with a callable head, 210 carrying a quote, 177 whose quote names an in-file declaration; the PRODUCTION PATH (getParser -> RealHaskellAnalyzer.analyze over 3,702/3,702 parsed, 0 failures) emits 177 decorates rows over 66 files — 1:1 with the census. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ON THE DECORATED DECLARATION, NEVER ON THE HEAD: TH decorators are library functions (`makeLenses`, `makePrisms`, `deriveJSON`) exactly as python's `@dataclass` is imported, so requiring an in-file head would exclude the construct; the census measured 0 in-file heads and 177 in-file decorated declarations, and 33 splices quoting an imported declaration are deliberately silent. THE DIRECTION IS THE LANE'S BRIEF: source = the enclosing module scope, target = the DECORATED declaration's own symbol, and the external decorator name rides in `metadata.decoratorName` so no edge targets a name nothing declares. `{-# ANN #-}` IS NOT THIS CONSTRUCT: 30 sites in 24 files (21 target `module`, 9 target a declared declaration) attach passive metadata and apply no callable, so they publish no edge and are disclosed as `metadata.annPragmaSites`. PART_OF IS THE TWELFTH IMPLEMENTED TYPE AND IT IS AN R3 EMISSION ON AN EXISTING NODE TYPE (the served grammar's `cpp` node; validation/m14/measurements/haskell-grammar-nodes.json, digest 37a6b07b1a83, 253 named of 552 ids — so R1 and R2 are UNNECESSARY and not taken, which is why this is an implementation and not a ruling). Haskell has no textual include of its own: `import Module` is a MODULE LOAD (it creates binding scope and is resolvable as `Module.item`), the OPPOSITE of a fragment, and stays `imports` (32,704 rows). The ONE textual-inclusion construct a Haskell file can carry is the C preprocessor's `#include` under `{-# LANGUAGE CPP #-}`: the named file's text is spliced into this module BEFORE parsing, it shares the module's single scope, and it has no module identity — the contract's part_of verbatim, and the fleet's implemented part_of set is unanimously textual file inclusion (cpp `#include`, fsharp `#load`, php include/require, erlang `-include`, typescript reference directives). MEASURED over the whole admitted population by inspection of every hit and by the production path (3,702/3,702 parsed, 0 failures): FOUR real directive sites, every one a quoted `#include `MachDeps.h`` (three Cabal Cmm test-suite Demo.hs files at :8, one hasura-engine Data/Atomic.hs at :19), and the production path emits exactly 4 part_of rows over 4 files — 1:1 with the census. The SEVEN other `#include` strings in the corpus are NOT directives and emit nothing (string-built include lines and the `-#include` ghc flag as a string, a Haddock mention, a JSON quasiquote body), all pinned as negatives by validation/m14/fixtures/haskell/part-of-cpp-include.hs. THE TARGET IS THE PART'S MODULE SYMBOL (the file STEM, symbol-shaped so the arbiter can bind it) and the written path is kept in `metadata.partPath`; every row carries the mandatory partRole library because this file is the unit and the directive names its part. `MachDeps.h` is a GHC system header, so its stem resolves to nothing in the admitted set — the system-header case the cpp lane handles, and the rows read unresolved/ext? rather than wrong. RENDERS AND MIXES_IN ARE THE TWO RULINGS ON THIS LANE (2026-10-27), each with a count over the same population and a measured falsifier, so the lane reads 12 of 12 applicable: `renders` has no component model (0 template-loader sites, and 4,201 quasiquote sites are markup producers rather than component renders); `mixes_in` has no member-set composition (0 of the 174 distinct named grammar types, and the 12,451 instances, 7,454 deriving clauses and 493 DerivingVia sites are conformance, which this lane already publishes as extends/implements/overrides). Both are pinned IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by validation/m14/fixtures/haskell/ruled-extended-types.hs, whose 0-count rows fail if a future rule fires on the shapes the language really has.

internal_silent._description: Grammar-internal containers, literals, comments/pragmas, and structural wrappers that correctly emit nothing (no relationship semantics in the analyzer's contract). |  is the analyzer evidenceClass STRING (real-haskell-analyzer.ts:972), not a grammar node type — moved 2026-09-03 after the F6 probe proved it never occurs in parses.
internal_silent._anonymous_tokens_note: THE 48-WAY SPLIT, MEASURED FROM THE PIN (2026-10-17): enumerating wasm/tree-sitter-haskell.wasm gives 552 node-type slots = 174 distinct NAMED + 293 distinct ANONYMOUS. 48 rows that had been sitting in `internal_silent.types` are, every one, in the ANONYMOUS set — the grammar produces them as literal tokens, not as named nodes — so none can be a section-A classification row. ZERO of the 48 is grammar DRIFT (no case/underscore-normalised spelling of any appears in the pin's named set) and ZERO is a spelling problem. Breakdown: 31 punctuation/operator literals, 14 keyword literals (data/type/foreign/hiding/where/of/if/then/else/in/stock/anyclass/nominal/default — tree-sitter spells keywords as anonymous literals), 3 single-letter anonymous tokens (d/e/p; `d` is a machinist template delimiter, see _m60hk_note). The analyzer never receives any of them as a named node; the construct is reached through the ENCLOSING named node (e.g. the wildcard `_` through the pattern node's own kind). They were removed from `types` and recorded in `_removed` because a row naming an anonymous token is not a classification of the grammar's named surface.
internal_silent._m60hk_note: M60-HK: `$`/`$$`/`d`/`ERROR` were classified after restoring the cabal corpus. `$` is the ordinary apply operator; `$$` and `d` are machinist template delimiters that appear because cabal ships .template.hs files, which are NOT valid Haskell (`$$name$$` placeholders); `ERROR` is the defensive parse-error node and only fires on those same 13 template/macro files. All four emit nothing, which is correct.
internal_silent._m60hk_note2: M60-HK, measured over the restored three-corpus sweep: %=65 '=34 stock=17 anyclass=17 ''=11 #=9 nominal=4 default=2 e=2 p=1. `%` and `'` are operators and type-level ticks and declare nothing. stock/anyclass/nominal are DeriveAnyClass strategies -- the same family as HS-G9's unhandled `via`, and likewise no symbol by design. `default` is a class default signature (HS-G7). ''/#/e/p occur only in cabal's machinist template files, which are not valid Haskell at all.

_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-haskell-analyzer.ts:132-133); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

gap._description: Advanced GHC-extension surfaces the analyzer does not model (declared limitations; bounded to extension syntax, not core Haskell). Differential floor target: Prelude/cabal corpora exercise few of these.

GADT-style data declarations emit no constructors/fields

Template Haskell splices/quotes: spliced declarations are invisible to the analyzer

pattern synonyms emit no symbols The restored `cabal` corpus has 96 `pattern` nodes across 50 files — the earlier "0 occurrences" was an artefact of the postgrest SUBSTITUTE corpus, which contains no pattern synonyms at all.

class defaults/fundeps/roles/kind signatures carry no metadata The grammar also emits the bare `role` and `representational` tokens (1 each), which HS-G7 did not list. The grammar also emits the bare `role` and `representational` tokens (1 each), which HS-G7 did not list.

design_decision.description: Haskell FP-family contract (HSD wave, probe-verified 2026-09-03): module-scoped symbols, class->Interface/instance->Class mapping, record/backtick/$/operator rulings.

decisions.question: record node in three positions: data declaration, body construction, update.
decisions.resolution: constructor-headed record in body position (parent chain crosses match/do/bind before any data_constructor) emits instantiates -> constructor; variable-headed record (update) emits nothing; records inside data_constructor emit Property symbols for fields only.

decisions.question: backtick infix (`x `elem2` xs`) was previously dropped entirely.
decisions.resolution: infix_id wraps the called function; if declared in-file (prepass set) a calls edge is emitted (HSD1).

decisions.question: infix with operator "$" is function application, not just syntax.
decisions.resolution: $ LHS (variable or qualified) resolves like an apply head and emits calls (HSD2); other operators only mark patterns (Monads/Functors/Pipe).

decisions.question: operator definitions `a +.+ b = ...` / `(<!>) f x = ...` were named by raw head text.
decisions.resolution: the symbol name is the OPERATOR text; operators enter the declared-function prepass so backtick/section uses resolve (HSD3).

decisions.question: parametrized instances `instance Sized [a]` lost their implements edge.
decisions.resolution: list in type_patterns resolves the instance target to [] (HSD4).

decisions.question: where/let locals: symbol scope and call attribution.
decisions.resolution: locals never become module symbols; a where-local function's internal calls attribute to the LOCAL function itself (go->local is a true edge); do-binds (`z <- fetch x`) are values, excluded from the callable prepass. SCOPED IDENTITY (2026-09-26, closes the bare-name caveat): a local's edge identity is its lexical owner chain (`owner.local`, nested `owner.inner.local`) and target resolution is lexical — a local is a candidate target only from inside its own scope, a shadowing binder wins for its whole RHS, and do-block `let` binders stay visible for the rest of the do block. Module-qualified targets are untouched.

decisions.question: type-position function nodes polluted the declared-function prepass with type variables (a, f, m) — fabricated calls.
decisions.resolution: function nodes carrying the parameter/result FIELD are type expressions and are skipped by the prepass; signature/internal function nodes likewise.

decisions.question: Haskell class/instance mapping onto the universal model.
decisions.resolution: class -> Interface, instance -> Class named by target type (universal impl-naming), signature inside class body -> Method owned by the Interface; instance methods are Functions owned by the instance Class.

decisions.question: #872 (F5 rotated-sample finding, Cabal-syntax FieldGrammar/Class.hs): which superclass heads emit extends? The old direct-apply + one-parens fallback missed tuple lists, applied heads (Eq (f a) => D f a), qualified heads (P.Show a), and quantified bodies (forall a. Applicative (f a)); the oracle shared the direct-apply blind spot and additionally over-emitted (descended into arguments).
decisions.resolution: RULED: the context is a CONSTRAINT TREE. Analyzer and oracle walk the same set of wrappers (context/tuple/parens/forall-body); an apply contributes its LEFT-SPINE head — name, constructor, or qualified (verbatim dotted text) — as the superclass; type arguments never become classes. Fixture pins Mergeable2->Show/Eq + Applied->Eq (payload-and-complexity); mutants haskell/drop-tuple-superclass + haskell/apply-head-as-argument; both pinned corpora 100%/0/0 @200/186 after the fix.

decisions.node_type: exports, foreign_import, type_synomym, gadt_constructors, class_declarations, instance_declarations
decisions.question: M60-HK wave: five of the product's ten relationship types were never emitted by this lane (uses, imports, exports, overrides, and extends on a corpus with no class hierarchy), `overrides` was already in the AUDITED label set with zero rows from BOTH sides, and 4,510 `contains`/`references` edges had no second implementation to disagree with them.
decisions.resolution: imports: a module import is an `imports` edge, not `references` -- 2,119 of the lane's 2,126 `references` edges carried isHaskellImport, so the label was 99.7% a mislabel and only 7 edges (FFI entities) were real references. exports: the export list is the module's API surface and the names were already collected into ctx.exports but never published; only `export` nodes count, because the list interleaves Haddock comments and iterating every child published 39 edges whose target was a `--` comment. overrides: `instance C T where m ...` overrides `C.m`, compared against a class->methods pre-pass because declaration order is not guaranteed. uses: a type synonym uses the types on its right-hand side, `name`/`constructor` leaves only -- a `variable` in type position is a type PARAMETER and publishing it is the fabrication the declared-type contract forbids. deriveHaskellEdges now derives all ten independently, sharing no helper with the analyzer.
decisions.evidence: Direct oracle-vs-analyzer comparison over 208 real .hs files (the F5 sweep cannot run: both registered corpora are absent). 8,283 truth rows, 8,271 covered, 13 analyzer-only, 12 truth-only -- 99.71% agreement, per label. calls / instantiates / uses / references / exports / imports at 0 discrepancy; contains 3/9; implements 3/3; overrides 6 truth-only. 5 new mutants, one per relationship type added, all caught (17 total).

decisions.question: M60-HK: both registered haskell corpora (cabal, hledger) are absent from this machine, so the differential could not run at all and every coverage claim was unfalsifiable.
decisions.resolution: Primary corpus re-registered to `postgrest` — the only checkout on this box with any Haskell (207 tracked .hs files: the hasql library plus postgrest's own src). DISCLOSED AS A SUBSTITUTE, not a replacement: it is smaller than the 637 cabal files the lane originally measured and its .hs surface is a vendored database library, so it exercises less dialect. The second corpus is DECLARED ABSENT rather than retargeted, because postgrest is the only Haskell checkout and pointing both entries at it would count one corpus twice. haskell therefore runs single-corpus, the same position fsharp records for itself. What that costs: a defect with zero occurrences in postgrest cannot be exercised by a second dialect. Restoring cabal or hledger is the M12/M60 owner's call.
decisions.evidence: With the corpus registered the lane runs: postgrest 60-file sample, 2,120 truth edges, 2,120 covered (100%), 0 MISSING, 1 unexplained (0.1%). Whole-file oracle-vs-analyzer comparison over 209 files: 8,302 of 8,304 truth rows (99.98%), nine of ten labels at exactly zero discrepancy.
